approaches.approach_name: Event-driven framework with centralized event management
approaches.description: The system is organized around a single Event Manager and a single Event Queue that dispatch events in FIFO order while the framework remains responsible for coordinating event processing.

addressed_attributes.rationale: The framework is explicitly described as handling and processing events through component interaction, with a dedicated Event Manager and Event Queue supporting that core behavior.
Centralizing dispatch through one Event Manager and one Event Queue provides a controlled processing path that supports consistent handling of events.
A single event-management path and one queue create a uniform mechanism for event processing across the framework.

approaches.approach_name: Sequential FIFO event dispatch on a single processor
approaches.description: Events are processed sequentially on one processor, with dispatch constrained to first-come-first-served ordering and an idle-wait state until input arrives.

addressed_attributes.rationale: FIFO event dispatch and idle waiting describe the required operational behavior for accepting and processing events in order.
Processing events one at a time on a single processor reduces concurrency complexity and helps preserve predictable behavior.

approaches.approach_name: Tight coupling between framework and application logic
approaches.description: Application logic is embedded within framework components, and the Event Manager interacts directly with application handlers, making the framework and application highly inter-dependent.

addressed_attributes.rationale: Direct interaction between the framework and application handlers enables the framework to execute application behavior as part of event processing.
The architecture uses a single integrated framework/application structure rather than separate subsystems.

approaches.approach_name: Base handler with specialized handler extension
approaches.description: A base Handler component is extended by standard handlers and application-specific handlers so new event behavior can be added through specialization.

addressed_attributes.rationale: Extending a base Handler with standard and application-specific handlers allows the framework to accommodate different event behaviors.
New handler behavior can be introduced by adding or specializing handlers instead of changing the base component structure.

approaches.description: The framework is intended to be used by an application and to let application components utilize framework services, implying the framework is the reusable platform around which applications are built.

addressed_attributes.rationale: A framework meant to be used by an application and extended through its components supports different application usages.
The framework structure is presented as a reusable base that can be adapted for application-specific use.

gaps.description: The evidence does not explicitly confirm whether the system is intended to be treated as a classic event-driven architecture style or only as an event-processing framework with event-driven characteristics.
